I'm a fan of both the traditional circuit and street circuits. But, in my humble opinion, the current street circuits used world wide don't offer the level of excitement that they should. What city would you like to see hosting a new Formula 1 event with a street circuit? And what should the FIA and the designers do to make it interesting for you to watch
Where would you like to see a new F1 street circuit?

I'm not a big fan of temporary street circuits. I find the circuits too constraining and the barriers too close for good racing/passing.

I love the more permanent tracks like Montreal and Albert Park.

There is a way to have a sort of hybrid of a traditional circuit and a temporary street circuit by employing some very clever city and circuit planning, and making use of some of the existing infrastructure.

Bear with me here for a second. These could work in and around growing cities with a need for new interconnecting roads or highway interchanges.

So once you find one such area, you get the FIA and track design engineers to work with the local/regional government's engineers to design a series of interchanges, loops, and rings that - when combined with the existing network of roads - would make for a decent circuit.

The new, let's call them 'track' sections would be designed with the fast sweeping corners we love and also with room to add temporary chicanes.

For the GP, temporary stands and all the rest could be erected and the circuit will be closed off but the rest of the year these new roads can be used for normal vehicular traffic. Like getting two birds stoned at once.

Since these roads will actually be useable and could decrease congestion most of the year, it would be easy (read: easier) to convince local/regional governments to fork out part of the cash needed to build them. This also has the advantage of having a much lower up-front cost, when you compare it to building a permanent track.

This is an idea we've been pushing for a long time because it really could be the easiest way to bring F1 to new places without compromising the level of excitement too much.

/rant

Edit: I forgot to include some places so here we go. Due to the nature of this solution, you'd really need somewhere either in Europe where towns are clustered really close together around some bigger cities or a city elsewhere that is expanding rapidly. With that in mind, I would say Stockholm, Amsterdam, or Toronto

The counter argument is that any F1 event, being a race or a demo (of which i know more about pricing and revenues) does bring economic growth to a city.

They have a short, temporary burst of funding, most of which goes into the pockets of a few people who own the teams, stadiums/circuits, etc. Hasn't this year already had problems with keeping circuits because they don't bring in enough money?
